title: Redwood Private VPC Security Architecture Deep Dive w/ Haven Bank
summary: Detailed architecture deep dive for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) focusing on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, KMS/HSM key management, SOC 2 implications, audit log forwarding, and SSO/RBAC. Customer requests sample network diagrams, POC runbook, and security docs; agreed to follow up with diagrams and SOC2 report. Next step: schedule 1-week POC window for egress testing.
next_steps: Maya: Share private VPC runbook, SOC 2 report, and sample network diagram by 2026-12-24
Liam: Provide recommended iptables/security group rules + egress testing checklist by 2026-12-23
Daniel/Tyler: Confirm internal firewall change window for POC (requested week of 2027-01-04)
Priya: Spin up POC checklist and initial SOW draft for a 1-week egress/canary POC
action_items: Maya Chen: Send SOC 2 Type II attestation and redwood-private security runbook - due 2026-12-24
Liam O'Connor: Export example VPC routing table and NACL configs, include sample terraform snippets - due 2026-12-23
Priya Kapoor: Draft POC steps for ingress/egress test and data residency validation - due 2026-12-22
Haven - Daniel Park: Share current network diagram and proxy/firewall ACLs for review - due 2026-12-23
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-12-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood), Olivia Martinez (CISO, Haven Bank), Daniel Park (Cloud Architect), Sanjay Rao (Security Engineer), Eleanor Bishop (Procurement), Tyler Nguyen (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. We're gonna run through the Private VPC architecture, focus on network isolation, ingress/egress patterns, firewalling, and key management. I'll hand over to Liam for the architecture sketch.
[00:35] Liam: Cool thanks Maya. Quick note, feel free to interrupt, this is a technical deep dive. Start high level: Redwood Private runs in a customer VPC or on-prem cluster and we give you a control plane to manage deployments. For network isolation we recommend isolated subnets for control plane, compute nodes, and a dedicated management subnet for admin access.
[01:10] Olivia: Quick question, when you say control plane in customer VPC, is that fully customer-managed or does Redwood need any egress to your control plane outside our network?
[01:30] Maya: Good question. There are two modes: fully private (no outbound to Redwood control plane) using our private deployment package, and a hybrid where the control plane is customer-managed but some telemetry/updates may be optional egress to Redwood-hosted services. For the POC we can do fully air-gapped if needed.
[02:05] Sanjay: When you say air-gapped, are you packaging the binaries for on-prem? And do you support offline attestation for updates?
[02:25] Priya: Yes, we provide a signed installation bundle; updates can be delivered via your internal artifact repo. We support verifying signatures locally. For attestation, we can integrate with your software signing process; HSM-based signing is supported if you want the extra chain of custody.
[03:00] Daniel: Network: we use Palo Alto NGFW and have strict egress rules. We'll need to understand what endpoints (IPs/ports) Redwood needs for control plane (if any), and if the model runtime needs any network egress for license checks or telemetry.
[03:30] Liam: For the private option there are zero required outbound endpoints for inference traffic. Control plane telemetry is optional and goes to ephemeral endpoints we can list. For the hosted control plane mode, we give a whitelist of domains/IP ranges. We'll provide both domain FQDNs and CIDR ranges in the runbook.
[04:05] Olivia: Okay, show me the recommended subnet layout and how you handle ingress. We can't expose inference endpoints publicly.
[04:30] Liam: Recommended: no public ELB in front of model nodes. Use private NLBs or internal load balancers with mTLS to the application tier. For ingress you can front with your API gateway on a private subnet, terminate TLS there, and then do mTLS between your gateway and Redwood runtime. We recommend strict security groups and NACLs — deny by default, allow specific ports.
[05:10] Tyler: We run NAT gateways for egress, and a strict proxy for outbound HTTP. If we do fully private, do your worker nodes require internet egress for downloading model files?
[05:30] Priya: Model artifacts can be pre-staged in an internal object storage (S3-compatible) or baked into the node image. We also support serving from a private registry. For initial model provisioning you can push the model artifacts into the cluster; no external egress is required at runtime.
[06:05] Sanjay: How about KV cache, shared state? Any cross-VM traffic we need to open?
[06:20] Liam: KV cache traffic is intra-VPC. We use ephemeral TLS for internal RPC between nodes; you can enforce mTLS and firewall between tiers. If you're using multiple AZs, open the internal ports among subnets only. We'll provide a port matrix in the runbook.
[07:00] Olivia: Auditability is critical. How do we get audit logs? We want logs shipped to our Splunk/QRadar and also maintain retention per SOC 2 requirements.
[07:20] Priya: We stream audit logs (access, admin actions, model versions, API calls) to a customer-configured endpoint. Supported sinks: S3, syslog, or direct push to SIEM via an HTTPS collector. We can also deliver logs to an S3 bucket that you control and lifecycle them per your retention policy.
[08:00] Daniel: Are logs encrypted at rest and in transit? Where's the KMS boundary?
[08:15] Liam: All logs we store at rest in your account (for private deployments) are encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMKs) — either your cloud KMS or an HSM. In transit we use TLS 1.3. For hosted artifacts we use Redwood-managed KMS but we can arrange CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for Dedicated/private.
[09:00] Olivia: We require HSM-backed keys for any crypto ops tied to PII. Do you support Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM integrations?
[09:20] Priya: Yes, we support AWS CloudHSM/Azure Dedicated HSM and also integrate with on-prem HSM via PKCS#11. For private deployments the KMS operations can be proxied to your HSM. We also support envelope encryption so only the HSM does master key ops.
[10:00] Sanjay: Related, what about key rotation and key access auditing? We need proof of rotation and who performed operations.
[10:20] Liam: KMS audit trails are written to your logging sink. We log key usage, creation, and rotation events. Rotation can be automated or manual; we recommend a rotation policy (e.g., 90 days) and we record the rotation operation in the audit log with user identity (SAML principal) and timestamp.
[11:00] Maya: Quick note for procurement: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs for our control plane; private deployments adopt those controls but you will retain control of some responsibilities. I'll attach the attestation docs after the call.
[11:30] Eleanor: On the contract side we need to see the SOC2 report and also a security addendum on data residency. Please send those.
[11:45] Maya: Yes, we'll send.
[12:00] Tyler: Network egress: we'd like to capture and block any unexpected outbound to the public internet. Can Redwood runtime do allowlists and fail closed if outbound is detected?
[12:20] Liam: Yes, runtime respects network policy. If you have NACLs/SGs that block egress, any attempts to reach out will fail. We also have a network policy agent that can alert on unexpected connections; it emits alerts to syslog/SIEM. For extra safety we can disable optional telemetry modules.
[13:10] Daniel: Firewalling specifics — do you support integration with our NGFW for deep packet inspection, or do we need to NAT through a proxy?
[13:30] Priya: Both supported. If you want your NGFW inline for DPI, you can route traffic through it. For simpler setups, route via NAT/proxy. We'll provide traffic examples (IP/port) so you can author firewall rules without opening broad ranges.
[14:05] Olivia: Data residency — some models and logs need to remain within our EU region. Can you pin model storage and runtime to a specific region?
[14:25] Liam: Yes, you can configure region pins. For private deployment this is in your environment so it's naturally within your region. For Dedicated we offer region-specific capacity. We'll document the regional controls.
[15:00] Sanjay: SSO and RBAC — we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning. How granular is your RBAC? We need admin, ops, view-only, and auditor roles.
[15:20] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC maps SAML groups to roles; built-in roles include Admin, Operator, ReadOnly, Auditor, and there are custom role capabilities for restricting model deploy, cost visibility, and audit read. All admin actions are logged.
[16:00] Daniel: Does SCIM support provisioning of service accounts and machine principals? We want to issue short-lived certs for automation.
[16:15] Liam: We support service accounts via our internal identity service; they can be provisioned via SCIM or API and issue short-lived tokens. For mTLS we can provision certs that are rotated automatically.
[17:00] Olivia: For legal review we need a data flow diagram showing PII boundaries, encryption at rest/in transit, and key ownership.
[17:20] Maya: We'll include that in the packet. Expect a diagram showing control plane vs runtime, data-at-rest boundaries, and flows to your SIEM.
[17:45] Tyler: On-firewall port matrix — can you narrowly define ports? Some of our teams want to lock everything down to specific ephemeral ranges.
[18:00] Liam: We'll provide a full port matrix and example security group rules. Example: internal RPC 9000-9010 (TLS), metrics 9100, admin API 8443 locked to management subnet, egress DNS 53 (TCP/UDP) only to your resolver. We'll include terraform snippets.
[18:45] Sanjay: What about backup and snapshots? Are backups encrypted and stored in our accounts?
[19:00] Priya: Backups are stored in your S3 bucket for private deployments and encrypted with your CMK. For on-prem we can write to your object store. Snapshots include checksums and can be validated during restore.
[19:40] Daniel: DR scenario — if an AZ goes down, how fast can you failover? Any special networking considerations?
[19:55] Liam: We recommend multi-AZ placement. Failover is generally a few minutes for model replicas; routing via internal NLB rebalances. You'll need cross-AZ peering and open internal ports across AZ subnets.
[20:30] Olivia: One more: legal asked about subprocessor list — do you have a list specifying any third-party services used in private deployments?
[20:45] Maya: For private deployments, third-party subprocessors are minimal and typically customer-chosen (e.g., your cloud provider, your SIEM). For any Redwood-managed components we'll share a subprocessor list and include contractual commitments.
[21:10] Tyler: POC mechanics — we want to try egress-blocked inference and simulate a misconfigured firewall to see telemetry and alerting.
[21:30] Priya: Proposed POC: 1) Baseline: deploy Redwood runtime into a test VPC with sample model; 2) Pre-stage model artifacts; 3) Apply strict egress NACLs (deny all except internal); 4) Run inference workload and observe failures; 5) Verify alerts/logs forwarded to your SIEM; 6) Re-enable selective egress and validate. That should be doable in 1 week.
[22:15] Daniel: Sounds fine. We'll need exact runbook steps and the firewall change window.
[22:35] Maya: Action items captured, we'll send docs.
[23:00] Olivia: On encryption, do you support FIPS 140-2 validated crypto modules? We have that requirement for some payment-related keys.
[23:15] Liam: Yes, for KMS we can use HSM modules that are FIPS validated. For TLS we use openssl builds compatible with FIPS if required. We'll confirm specific module versions in the runbook.
[24:00] Sanjay: Any telemetry that contains PII we need to mask before leaving our environment — can you support scrubbers?
[24:20] Priya: Yes, we support configurable scrubbing rules and PII redaction for logs and traces prior to sending. For private/on-prem you can also opt to disable telemetry completely.
[25:00] Daniel: Regarding RBAC — auditors need read-only access to audit logs without edit rights. Is that a built-in role?
[25:20] Liam: Yes, Auditor role exists and is read-only for logs and configuration snapshots.
[26:00] Maya: Procurement question — pricing for private deployment and support tiers, will that be part of the next email? Eleanor?
[26:15] Eleanor: Yes we'll want a line item for HSM integration and extra support SLA.
[26:40] Maya: We'll include that in the SOW.
[27:00] Tyler: Small gotcha — our NGFW blocks SRV DNS and some internal service discovery; if you rely on service discovery we need static endpoints.
[27:20] Liam: We can provide static endpoints and recommend avoiding multicast. We'll give a static list of IPs and hostnames for the POC.
[28:00] Olivia: Any compliance mappings — can you show controls mapped to SOC 2 and ISO 27001?
[28:20] Maya: Yes, we'll include a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to SOC2 categories, plus customer responsibilities for private deployments.
[29:00] Sanjay: For lifecycle — how do you handle deprovisioning of data when a tenant is offboarded?
[29:15] Priya: We run a guaranteed wipe that removes model caches and data; we provide a certificate of destruction and logs showing the wipe steps and timestamps. For persistent storage in your object store, you control deletion lifecycle; we provide scripts to automate it.
[30:00] Daniel: Are there any default privileged accounts or backdoors? I need to be explicit for the audit team.
[30:20] Liam: No backdoors. Admin access is via RBAC and SAML; Redwood engineers do not have standing administrative accounts inside customer-private VPCs unless you grant them temporary access via a just-in-time mechanism which is logged and auditable.
[31:00] Olivia: That addresses the big ones. Can you summarize the deliverables?
[31:20] Maya: Sure: 1) Network diagram and port matrix; 2) SOC 2 attestation and controls matrix; 3) Private deployment runbook with TF snippets; 4) POC SOW and steps for egress test; 5) KMS/HSM integration guide. We'll send all by 2026-12-24.
[31:55] Eleanor: We'll need those to be part of our packet to legal. Thanks.
[32:10] Maya: Anything else?
[32:20] Daniel: One minor thing — can we get an example of audit events schema so we can map fields into our SIEM?
[32:35] Priya: Yes, we'll attach an example JSON schema for audit events and sample log entries.
[33:00] Sanjay: Can we also get a list of default telemetry fields (latency, model_id, prompt_hash) so we can ensure no sensitive payloads are sent?
[33:20] Liam: We'll provide that; telemetry omits raw prompt text unless you enable it. By default we send prompt hashes and metadata.
[34:00] Olivia: Good. If we wanted to use customer-managed egress proxies for model downloads, any extra auth needed?
[34:20] Priya: We'll support signed URLs, IAM roles, or mutual TLS to authenticate to your object store. We'll include samples for each.
[35:00] Tyler: POC timeline preference: week of Jan 4th. We'll confirm.
[35:15] Maya: Noted.
[36:00] Liam: One more technical: internal service mesh compatibility — if you run Istio/linkerd do we interfere?
[36:20] Priya: We work with service meshes; we recommend sidecar-less setup for model nodes to reduce latency, but we can integrate with mesh for admin/control plane traffic. We'll provide recommended annotations to avoid mTLS duplication.
[37:00] Daniel: Can you support VPC peering as an option rather than Transit Gateway?
[37:15] Liam: Yes, peering is supported for small-scale setups; for many VPCs transit gateway or private link is cleaner. We'll outline tradeoffs.
[38:00] Olivia: Anything about packet capture for forensics?
[38:12] Priya: We don't capture packet payloads by default. For forensics you can enable packet mirroring to your collector; we can help define retention and access controls.
[38:50] Sanjay: Final question — are model weights considered customer data for retention controls?
[39:05] Liam: Model weights are treated as artifacts; if you bring your own models they are stored in your storage and subject to your retention policies. If Redwood manages them we can store them in your account with CMK.
[39:40] Maya: Great. I'll send the deliverables and a proposed SOW for the POC. Any blockers?
[39:55] Daniel: We'll check internal calendar for firewall windows, but no blockers on principle.
[40:10] Eleanor: Procurement will expect pricing for HSM and longer-term support.
[40:30] Maya: We'll include it.
[41:00] Olivia: Thank you all, this was productive.
[41:10] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and next steps.

Notes/Imperfect transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some acronyms mis-heard (e.g., NGLW -> NGFW), and a few technical terms spelled phonetically.

End of transcript.
